\subsection{U15: A non-linear formula's integer division is Stan's in the model and R's in the predictions: \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1 /\allowbreak{} 2) *\allowbreak{} a} fits mu = 0 and predicts a / 2}
\label{U15}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: bf(..., nl = TRUE), posterior\_epred(). Wrong result; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] C02 (\#52); divergence D61.
\item[What] The expression is written into the Stan program as it stands, where \texttt{1 /\allowbreak{} 2} of two integer literals is integer division (0), and evaluated in R for predictions, where it is 0.5.
\item[Observed] \texttt{bf(\allowbreak{}y \textasciitilde{} (\allowbreak{}1 /\allowbreak{} 2) *\allowbreak{} a,\allowbreak{} a \textasciitilde{} 1,\allowbreak{} nl =\allowbreak{} TRUE)}, y = 1, a = 2, sigma = 1: the model's log likelihood is -1.418938533204673 (that of mu = 0); \texttt{posterior\_\allowbreak{}epred(\allowbreak{})} gives 1 (mu = 0.5 a).
\item[Expected] One meaning in both: as R reads the formula, mu = 1 and the log likelihood -0.9189385332046728.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U15.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U15.out}.
\item[Fix] Write numeric literals into the Stan program as reals (\texttt{1} as \texttt{1.\allowbreak{}0}), so that Stan divides as R does, or refuse an integer division in a non-linear formula.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not found in brms's NEWS or the issue tracker (read-only searches, 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23).
\end{description}

\subsection{U16: Functions Stan does not have (\texttt{plogis(\allowbreak{})}, and \texttt{gp(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{mo(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{ar(\allowbreak{})} written in the expression) pass into a non-linear model's program unchecked}
\label{U16}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: bf(..., nl = TRUE), make\_stancode(), brm(). Missing validation; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] C02, C04 (\#52, \#53); divergence D61, D70.
\item[What] brms writes the expression into the program without checking its functions, so the user gets a Stan semantic error instead of a message from brms (and \texttt{plogis(\allowbreak{})}, which brms's R-side predictions evaluate, is not translated to \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}logit}).
\item[Observed] \texttt{y \textasciitilde{} plogis(\allowbreak{}a *\allowbreak{} x)}, \texttt{y \textasciitilde{} a *\allowbreak{} gp(\allowbreak{}x)}, \texttt{y \textasciitilde{} a *\allowbreak{} mo(\allowbreak{}z)}, \texttt{y \textasciitilde{} a +\allowbreak{} ar(\allowbreak{}t)}: brms generates a program; Stan's compiler: "A returning function was expected but an undeclared identifier 'plogis' was supplied" (and 'gp', 'mo', 'ar').
\item[Expected] A refusal from brms naming the function and what to write instead (or a translation of \texttt{plogis} to \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}logit}); the control \texttt{y \textasciitilde{} inv\_\allowbreak{}logit(\allowbreak{}a *\allowbreak{} x)} compiles.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U16.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U16.out}.
\item[Fix] Check each function name of a non-linear formula against the functions Stan and brms's Stan code provide before generating code, translating R's \texttt{plogis}, \texttt{qlogis}, \texttt{pnorm} to \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}logit}, \texttt{logit}, \texttt{Phi} or refusing with a message, and refuse \texttt{gp(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{mo(\allowbreak{})}, \texttt{ar(\allowbreak{})} inside the expression with a pointer to the parameter formulas.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not found in brms's NEWS or the issue tracker (read-only searches, 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23).
\end{description}

\subsection{U17: Under identity and inverse links a non-positive mean is returned by \texttt{posterior\_\allowbreak{}epred(\allowbreak{})} without a word, and \texttt{posterior\_\allowbreak{}predict(\allowbreak{})} draws NaN}
\label{U17}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: posterior\_epred(), posterior\_predict(), negbinomial("identity"), Gamma("inverse"), Gamma("identity"), inverse.gaussian("1/mu\textasciicircum{}2"). Missing validation; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] E06, E02 (\#71, \#75); divergence D134, D115.
\item[What] Stan rejects a draw whose mean leaves the family's support, but on new rows brms returns that mean as an expected value and draws NaN responses with only R's random-number warning. \texttt{Gamma(\allowbreak{}"inverse")} is the Gamma family's default link.
\item[Observed] b\_Intercept = 1, b\_x = 1, new row x = -2.33 (eta = -1.33): negbinomial identity and Gamma identity \texttt{posterior\_\allowbreak{}epred} -1.33, Gamma inverse -0.75188, each with no error or warning; inverse.gaussian 1/mu\textasciicircum{}2 NaN (R's "NaNs produced"); \texttt{posterior\_\allowbreak{}predict} NaN or NA with R's "NAs produced" / "NaNs produced".
\item[Expected] An error, or NA with a warning naming the rows whose mean is outside the family's support (mu \textgreater{} 0; eta \textgreater{} 0 under 1/mu\textasciicircum{}2).
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U17.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U17.out}.
\item[Fix] Check the predicted mean against the family's support in \texttt{posterior\_\allowbreak{}epred(\allowbreak{})} and \texttt{posterior\_\allowbreak{}predict(\allowbreak{})} (mu \textgreater{} 0 for the negative binomial, Gamma and inverse Gaussian; eta \textgreater{} 0 for the 1/mu\textasciicircum{}2 link) and stop, or return NA with a warning that names the rows, as for any other invalid input.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not found in brms's NEWS or the issue tracker (read-only searches, 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23).
\end{description}

\subsection{U18: asym\_laplace accepts a fixed quantile of 0 or 1, where the density is 0 everywhere}
\label{U18}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: asym\_laplace(), bf(..., quantile = ). Missing validation; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] E02 (\#75); divergence D115.
\item[What] brms refuses a fixed quantile outside [0, 1] but accepts the end points, where the asymmetric Laplace density \texttt{q (\allowbreak{}1 -\allowbreak{} q) /\allowbreak{} sigma *\allowbreak{} exp(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{})} is 0 for every response, so the model has log density -Inf everywhere.
\item[Observed] \texttt{make\_\allowbreak{}standata(\allowbreak{}bf(\allowbreak{}y \textasciitilde{} 1,\allowbreak{} quantile =\allowbreak{} 0))} and \texttt{quantile =\allowbreak{} 1}: accepted (1.5: refused, "Parameter 'quantile' must be between 0 and 1."); \texttt{dasym\_\allowbreak{}laplace(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} quantile =\allowbreak{} 0)} = 0, 0, 0; \texttt{log\_\allowbreak{}prob} of the compiled model: -Inf.
\item[Expected] Refuse quantile = 0 and 1 as well: the parameter must lie strictly between 0 and 1.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U18.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U18.out}.
\item[Fix] Require \texttt{0 \textless{} quantile \textless{} 1} for a fixed quantile (the open interval), with the same message.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not found in brms's NEWS or the issue tracker (read-only searches, 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23).
\end{description}

\subsection{U19: The default length-scale prior of \texttt{gp(\allowbreak{})} is solved to a tolerance coarser than the 6 decimals it is printed and written with}
\label{U19}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: gp() default lscale prior, get\_prior(), default\_prior(). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] C03 (\#51); divergence D67. Rounding only: the prior differs from the correctly rounded one in the 6th decimal.
\item[What] The default \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}gamma(\allowbreak{}a,\allowbreak{} b)} puts 1\% of the mass below the smallest scaled distance between distinct inputs and 1\% above the largest; brms's solver stops within about 1e-7 of the solution, which crosses a rounding boundary at some inputs.
\item[Observed] x = (0, 0.5, 1): \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}gamma(\allowbreak{}45.\allowbreak{}631904,\allowbreak{} 31.\allowbreak{}399697)}; x = (0, 0.48188060200668892, 1): \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}gamma(\allowbreak{}41.\allowbreak{}190626,\allowbreak{} 27.\allowbreak{}743173)}. (x = (0, 0.3, 1) agrees.)
\item[Expected] The solutions 45.631904608850, 31.399697537363 and 41.190626321252, 27.743173538338 round to \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}gamma(\allowbreak{}45.\allowbreak{}631905,\allowbreak{} 31.\allowbreak{}399698)} and \texttt{inv\_\allowbreak{}gamma(\allowbreak{}41.\allowbreak{}190626,\allowbreak{} 27.\allowbreak{}743174)}.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U19.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U19.out}.
\item[Fix] Solve the one equation in the shape to double precision before rounding: with \texttt{1 /\allowbreak{} l \textasciitilde{} Gamma(\allowbreak{}a,\allowbreak{} rate b)}, \texttt{b =\allowbreak{} hi *\allowbreak{} qgamma(\allowbreak{}0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} a)} and \texttt{pgamma(\allowbreak{}hi *\allowbreak{} qgamma(\allowbreak{}0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} a) /\allowbreak{} lo,\allowbreak{} a) =\allowbreak{} 0.\allowbreak{}99} (bracketed root finding to about 1e-14), or write the unrounded values into the model.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not found in brms's NEWS or the issue tracker (read-only searches, 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23).
\end{description}

\subsection{U20: Approximate GP \texttt{gp(\allowbreak{}x,\allowbreak{} k =\allowbreak{} )}: NaN gradient wherever the spectral density underflows (every lscale above about 1 with k = 30)}
\label{U20}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: gp(x, k = , c = ) (generated Stan code: sqrt of the spectral density). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] C03 (\#51); divergence D66. The divergence row records this as not probed; reproduced here.
\item[What] Basis function j is weighted by \texttt{sqrt(\allowbreak{}S(\allowbreak{}w\_\allowbreak{}j))}, \texttt{S(\allowbreak{}w) =\allowbreak{} sdgp\textasciicircum{}2 sqrt(\allowbreak{}2 pi) lscale exp(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}lscale\textasciicircum{}2 w\textasciicircum{}2 /\allowbreak{} 2)}. Where S underflows to 0 (\texttt{lscale *\allowbreak{} w\_\allowbreak{}j} above about 38.6) the log density is finite but the chain rule through \texttt{sqrt} at 0 gives Inf times 0 = NaN in the gradient of sdgp and lscale. With k = 30 and c = 5/4 that is every lscale above 1.024 on brms's scaled inputs, an ordinary length-scale for a smooth function, where HMC cannot move.
\item[Observed] \texttt{y \textasciitilde{} gp(\allowbreak{}x,\allowbreak{} k =\allowbreak{} 30,\allowbreak{} c =\allowbreak{} 5/\allowbreak{}4)}, 12 rows: at lscale = 1.2 and 2 the log density is finite (-58.82, -62.71) and the gradient in (log sdgp, log lscale) is (NaN, NaN), 2 of the 34 entries; at lscale = 0.5 all entries agree with a finite difference to 7e-9.
\item[Expected] The finite gradient (4.3837865, -4.6773439) at lscale = 1.2 and (1.9224068, -9.2924243) at 2 (central finite differences of brms's own \texttt{log\_\allowbreak{}prob}; the other 32 entries agree to 7e-9).
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U20.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U20.out}.
\item[Fix] Form the weight without a square root of an underflowed number: \texttt{sqrt(\allowbreak{}S(\allowbreak{}w)) =\allowbreak{} sdgp (\allowbreak{}2 pi)\textasciicircum{}(\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}4) sqrt(\allowbreak{}lscale) exp(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}lscale\textasciicircum{}2 w\textasciicircum{}2 /\allowbreak{} 4)} (or \texttt{exp(\allowbreak{}0.\allowbreak{}5 *\allowbreak{} log S)} with \texttt{log S} computed directly), whose gradient is finite (and 0 in the limit) where S underflows.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not found in brms's NEWS or the issue tracker (read-only searches, 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23).
\end{description}

\subsection{U21: Priors on probability parameters (zi, hu, zoi, coi) are renormalised on (0, 1): divergence row D29 is not what brms does}
\label{U21}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: zero\_inflated\_poisson() zi prior, zero\_one\_inflated\_beta() zoi and coi priors (lprior). Wrong result; not a bug after all. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] B06 (\#39); divergence D29. Checked for this log; the row's statement was not a brms output.
\item[What] D29 says a prior on \texttt{zi} / \texttt{hu} is added as written, not renormalised on (0, 1). brms 2.23.0's \texttt{lprior} divides each such prior by its mass on (0, 1), as it does for the lower-bounded classes, so there is nothing to report upstream. Kept so the row is not reported by mistake.
\item[Observed] zi \textasciitilde{} normal(0.5, 1) at 0.3 with the Intercept at 0.2: lprior -2.50819864514782; zoi \textasciitilde{} normal(0.3, 0.1), coi \textasciitilde{} logistic(0, 1), phi \textasciitilde{} exponential(1): -3.27907096338989.
\item[Expected] Renormalised on (0, 1): -2.50819864514782 and -3.27907096338989, equal (as written they would be -3.46811497884345 and -4.74550578682117).
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U21.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U21.out}.
\item[Fix] None in brms. Divergence row D29 now says that brms renormalises these priors on (0, 1).
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not applicable (not a bug).
\end{description}

\subsection{U22: Stan's \texttt{normal\_\allowbreak{}lccdf} loses its value in the upper tail (-Inf from z of about 8.3), so brms's right-censored rows are -Inf and truncated rows +Inf}
\label{U22}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] Stan Math: normal\_lccdf, brms: gaussian() with cens() (right-censored rows) and trunc(lb = ). Wrong result; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] B02 (\#40); divergence D24, D25. The value loss beyond z of about 5 and the -Inf from 8.3 were measured for this log; the divergence rows record the gradient (U23).
\item[What] \texttt{normal\_\allowbreak{}lccdf(\allowbreak{}z \textbar{} 0,\allowbreak{} 1)} = log(1 - Phi(z)) is off by 2.6e-12 relative at z = 5, 2.1e-9 at 6.17, 5.3e-4 at 8 and -Inf from about 8.3, where the value is an ordinary number. brms calls it for a right-censored Gaussian row and for a truncation's lower bound, so such a row 8.3 SD above its mean has log density -Inf, and a row of \texttt{y \textbar{} trunc(\allowbreak{}lb =\allowbreak{} L)} with L 9 SD above the mean has log density +Inf (its density minus -Inf).
\item[Observed] Right-censored rows at mu = 0, sigma = 1: z = 5 -15.0649983940277, z = 8 -35.03205247743868, z = 8.3, 9 and 20 -Inf. Truncated rows y = L + 0.5 of \texttt{y \textbar{} trunc(\allowbreak{}lb =\allowbreak{} L)}: L = 6.17 -1.365568612357809, L = 8 -2.011886055765999, L = 9 +Inf.
\item[Expected] R's \texttt{pnorm(\allowbreak{}z,\allowbreak{} lower.\allowbreak{}tail =\allowbreak{} FALSE,\allowbreak{} log.\allowbreak{}p =\allowbreak{} TRUE)}: -15.06499839398873, -35.01343715991455, -37.49421742374825, -43.62814911333211, -203.9171553710973; truncated rows -1.365568567117943, -2.030501373290122, -2.41578941987256. Controls (z = 0, 1; L = 0, 1) agree to 1e-15.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U22.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U22.out}.
\item[Fix] Evaluate the upper tail through the lower one, \texttt{normal\_\allowbreak{}lccdf(\allowbreak{}y \textbar{} mu,\allowbreak{} sigma) =\allowbreak{} std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}y -\allowbreak{} mu) /\allowbreak{} sigma)} (Stan's \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf} is exact in value to -40 in these probes), or from \texttt{log(\allowbreak{}erfc(\allowbreak{}z /\allowbreak{} sqrt 2) /\allowbreak{} 2)} with \texttt{erfc} (or \texttt{erfcx}) rather than \texttt{1 -\allowbreak{} erf}. brms can do the first today for any Stan version.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math}
\item[Known upstream] Known and fixed in Stan Math 5.4.0.
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/1985} (closed 2026-08-30): Accuracy of normal\_lccdf much worse than normal\_lcdf
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3363} (merged 2026-08-30): Aligned normal\_lccdf and std\_normal\_lccdf with the lcdf functions
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/2847} (closed 2026-10-07): Errors when right-censoring: bug in normal\_lccdf?
\\ Fixed in: Stan Math 5.4.0 (released 2026-09-16), which rstan 2.32.7 with StanHeaders 2.32.10 does not include; which StanHeaders release ships it was not checked.
\\ brms issue \#1956 (open) notes that \texttt{normal\_\allowbreak{}lccdf} saturates earlier than \texttt{normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf} in its discussion of two-sided truncation.
\end{description}

\subsection{U23: Stan's \texttt{normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf} / \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf} derivative is inexact (up to 2.3e-5 relative), and so are brms's censored Gaussian gradients}
\label{U23}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] Stan Math: normal\_lcdf, std\_normal\_lcdf, normal\_lccdf (upper tail), brms: gaussian() with cens() and trunc(). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] B02 (\#40); divergence D24, D25. \texttt{gauss\_\allowbreak{}censored} and \texttt{gauss\_\allowbreak{}truncated} are accepted against 50-digit references for their gradients (P6, \#47).
\item[What] The value of log Phi(z) is accurate, but its derivative is not the inverse Mills ratio phi(z) / Phi(z) to double precision: it is off by 7e-7 at z = 1, 6.4e-6 at 2, 2.3e-5 at -10 and 1.3e-5 at -38, as if from a separate approximation; \texttt{normal\_\allowbreak{}lccdf}'s derivative is off by 4.5e-8 at z = 6.17 and 1.9\% at 8. brms's left- and right-censored (and truncated) Gaussian rows differentiate through them.
\item[Observed] Gradient in (mu, log sigma) of one censored row at mu = 0, sigma = 1: left-censored z = -10: (-10.0978573856826, 100.978573856826); z = 2: (-0.0552482144761343, -0.1104964289522686); right-censored z = 8: (8.273965879706052, 66.19172703764842).
\item[Expected] (-10.09809323396249, 100.9809323396249), (-0.05524786267898995, -0.1104957253579799) and (8.121368112236123, 64.97094489788898), from \texttt{m(\allowbreak{}z) =\allowbreak{} exp(\allowbreak{}dnorm(\allowbreak{}z,\allowbreak{} log =\allowbreak{} TRUE) -\allowbreak{} pnorm(\allowbreak{}z,\allowbreak{} log.\allowbreak{}p =\allowbreak{} TRUE))}; the right-censored row at z = 0 agrees to 1.4e-16. On the frozen cases: up to 2.5e-6 (\texttt{gauss\_\allowbreak{}censored}) and 4.2e-7 (\texttt{gauss\_\allowbreak{}truncated}) relative.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U23.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U23.out}.
\item[Fix] Differentiate the accurate value instead of an approximation: \texttt{d/\allowbreak{}dz log Phi(\allowbreak{}z) =\allowbreak{} phi(\allowbreak{}z) /\allowbreak{} Phi(\allowbreak{}z) =\allowbreak{} sqrt(\allowbreak{}2 /\allowbreak{} pi) /\allowbreak{} erfcx(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}z /\allowbreak{} sqrt 2)} (with \texttt{erfcx}, now a Stan Math function), or \texttt{exp(\allowbreak{}log phi(\allowbreak{}z) -\allowbreak{} log Phi(\allowbreak{}z))} from the same log CDF the value uses.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math}
\item[Known upstream] Not found as a report of the derivative's accuracy; an open pull request reworks std\_normal\_lcdf.
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3406} (open PR): Expanded numerical stability and performance for \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf}, reused across distributions \& functions
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/2881} (open): normal\_lcdf and normal\_lccdf give infinite gradients for infinite inputs.
\\ Whether PR \#3406 makes the derivative exact was not checked (its code was not read).
\end{description}

\subsection{U24: cumulative("probit") through Stan's \texttt{ordered\_\allowbreak{}probit\_\allowbreak{}lpmf}: exact log density, gradient off by up to 1.2e-5 relative}
\label{U24}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] Stan Math: ordered\_probit\_lpmf, brms: cumulative(link = "probit"). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] D04 (\#64); divergence D88. Accepted with a 50-digit reference for the gradient (P6, \#66).
\item[What] brms writes the cumulative probit likelihood with Stan's \texttt{ordered\_\allowbreak{}probit\_\allowbreak{}lpmf} (the generated program calls it). Its value equals the exact log likelihood to 2e-16, but its gradient in the thresholds does not; size and pattern match U23's \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf} derivative, which Stan issue \#2228 says \texttt{ordered\_\allowbreak{}probit} uses (a likely common cause, not verified from Stan's code).
\item[Observed] One row per category, thresholds (-2, 0.5, 2.5): gradient (-1.1103089658908, -8.506981885742, -5.5295205825131), 1.2e-5 relative off; (-1, 1, 2): 2.4e-6; (-6, -4.5, 0.3): 7.2e-6. On the frozen case \texttt{cumulative\_\allowbreak{}probit\_\allowbreak{}varint}: up to 6.5e-5, at 173 of 176 entries.
\item[Expected] (-1.1103226460712, -8.5069986883767, -5.5295340249966), from \texttt{phi(\allowbreak{}t\_\allowbreak{}k) /\allowbreak{} P} and \texttt{-\allowbreak{}phi(\allowbreak{}t\_\allowbreak{}\{k-\allowbreak{}1\}) /\allowbreak{} P} through Stan's ordered transform; the log densities (-10.46347710031321, -8.001719394174177, -34.77299757782713) agree to 2e-16.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U24.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U24.out}.
\item[Fix] Differentiate \texttt{log(\allowbreak{}Phi(\allowbreak{}b) -\allowbreak{} Phi(\allowbreak{}a))} exactly: \texttt{d/\allowbreak{}db =\allowbreak{} phi(\allowbreak{}b) /\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}Phi(\allowbreak{}b) -\allowbreak{} Phi(\allowbreak{}a))}, \texttt{d/\allowbreak{}da =\allowbreak{} -\allowbreak{}phi(\allowbreak{}a) /\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}Phi(\allowbreak{}b) -\allowbreak{} Phi(\allowbreak{}a))}, each ratio as \texttt{exp(\allowbreak{}log phi -\allowbreak{} log mass)} with the mass from the tail both arguments lie in; with U23 fixed (an exact derivative of \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf}) this may follow.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math}
\item[Known upstream] Not found as such; related work on std\_normal\_lcdf is open.
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/2228} (closed 2020-12-09): Use std\_normal\_lc(c)df functions for the ordered\_probit distribution
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3406} (open PR): Expanded numerical stability and performance for \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf}, reused across distributions \& functions
\end{description}

\subsection{U25: Stan's \texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}lccdf} derivative in the shape is inexact (up to 1.2e-2 relative), and so are brms's right-censored Gamma gradients}
\label{U25}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] Stan Math: gamma\_lccdf, brms: Gamma() with cens() (right-censored rows). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] E04 (\#77); divergence D120. \texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}censored\_\allowbreak{}interval} is accepted with a 50-digit reference for its gradient (P6, \#78).
\item[What] The value of log Q(shape, x) is right, and so is \texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}lcdf}'s shape derivative (to 1e-10), but \texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}lccdf}'s shape derivative is not: brms's right-censored Gamma rows (\texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}lccdf}, rate = shape / mu) have inexact gradients in log(shape). brms's interval rows use \texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}lcdf} and are accurate here.
\item[Observed] Gradient in (log mu, log shape) of one right-censored row: y = 7, mu = 5, shape = 5: (3.691412255656, -0.4868664317708), 1.2e-2 relative off in log(shape); y = 2, mu = 5, shape = 10: 2.5e-4; y = 3, mu = 2, shape = 2: 6.1e-5. On the frozen case \texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}censored\_\allowbreak{}interval}: up to 2.8e-5.
\item[Expected] (3.691412255645, -0.4809855583225), 0.02945472493298 and -0.2673022227384 in log(shape), from fourth-order differences of R's \texttt{pgamma(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} lower.\allowbreak{}tail =\allowbreak{} FALSE,\allowbreak{} log.\allowbreak{}p =\allowbreak{} TRUE)} (accurate to about 1e-11); the left-censored and interval rows agree to 1e-10.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U25.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U25.out}.
\item[Fix] Compute the shape derivative of log Q(a, x) to double precision, e.g. from the derivative of log P (series for x \textless{} a + 1, \texttt{dQ/\allowbreak{}da =\allowbreak{} -\allowbreak{}dP/\allowbreak{}da}) and the continued fraction of Q differentiated through its recurrence above, iterated to machine precision; or by quadrature of \texttt{int\_\allowbreak{}x\textasciicircum{}inf log(\allowbreak{}t) t\textasciicircum{}(\allowbreak{}a -\allowbreak{} 1) exp(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}t) dt}.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math}
\item[Known upstream] Known: the incomplete gamma gradients are an open Stan Math issue, with work merged since StanHeaders 2.32 and an open pull request.
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/2006} (open): gamma\_p and gamma\_q gradient problems
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3408} (open PR): Incomplete gamma gradient roots and log-space cdfs for six distributions
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/3257} (closed 2026-04-16): Fix \texttt{gamma\_\allowbreak{}lccdf} actually
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3275} (merged 2026-04-16): Fix gamma lccdf
\\ Whether the gamma\_lccdf rework merged in 2026 (first in Stan Math 5.3.0) makes the shape derivative exact was not checked; nothing newer than StanHeaders 2.32.10 could be installed.
\end{description}

\subsection{U26: Stan's \texttt{von\_\allowbreak{}mises\_\allowbreak{}lpdf} overflows (\texttt{cyl\_\allowbreak{}bessel\_\allowbreak{}i} numeric overflow) for kappa above about 713.9}
\label{U26}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] Stan Math: von\_mises\_lpdf, brms: von\_mises(). Wrong result; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] E02 (\#75); divergence D113.
\item[What] The density's normalising constant I0(kappa) is evaluated itself and overflows, so \texttt{log\_\allowbreak{}prob} raises an error (and a fit cannot start) for a precision above about 713.9, where the density is ordinary. brms's R-side \texttt{dvon\_\allowbreak{}mises} (log\_lik) is exact there.
\item[Observed] One row y = 0.1 at mu = 0: kappa = 700 and 713 within 8.4e-14 of the exact value; kappa = 714, 720, 1000: "Exception: Error in function boost::math::cyl\_bessel\_i\textless{}double\textgreater{}(double,double): numeric overflow".
\item[Expected] \texttt{kappa (\allowbreak{}cos(\allowbreak{}y -\allowbreak{} mu) -\allowbreak{} 1) -\allowbreak{} log(\allowbreak{}2 pi) -\allowbreak{} log(\allowbreak{}i0e(\allowbreak{}kappa))}: -1.200698236329766, -1.226487658870219, -2.46102067825299 (R's \texttt{besselI(\allowbreak{}kappa,\allowbreak{} 0,\allowbreak{} expon.\allowbreak{}scaled =\allowbreak{} TRUE)}).
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U26.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U26.out}.
\item[Fix] Never form I0(kappa): \texttt{log I0(\allowbreak{}kappa) =\allowbreak{} kappa +\allowbreak{} log(\allowbreak{}i0e(\allowbreak{}kappa))} with the exponentially scaled Bessel function (or the large-kappa asymptotic series), so the log density is \texttt{kappa (\allowbreak{}cos(\allowbreak{}y -\allowbreak{} mu) -\allowbreak{} 1) -\allowbreak{} log(\allowbreak{}2 pi) -\allowbreak{} log(\allowbreak{}i0e(\allowbreak{}kappa))}.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math}
\item[Known upstream] Probably fixed upstream: a von\_mises\_lpdf stability fix merged in 2024 (not verified against this overflow).
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/3035} (closed 2024-03-23): Improve numerical stability of von\_mises\_lpdf
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3036} (merged 2024-03-23): Improve numerical stability of von\_mises\_lpdf
\\ \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/1633} (closed 2024-08-13): use von\_mises\_lpdf directly instead of von\_mises2\_lpdf after next stan update
\\ Fixed in: probably Stan Math 4.9.0 (2024-06-03), later than the Stan Math in StanHeaders 2.32.10; not verified, since nothing newer could be installed.
\end{description}

\subsection{U27: Stan's \texttt{skew\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lpdf} and \texttt{exp\_\allowbreak{}mod\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lpdf} are -Inf once their normal-CDF factor underflows (argument below about -37.5)}
\label{U27}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] Stan Math: skew\_normal\_lpdf, exp\_mod\_normal\_lpdf, brms: skew\_normal(), brms: exgaussian(). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] D01 (\#60); divergence D77. D01's probes used rstan::expose\_stan\_functions; here the same comes from brms models.
\item[What] Both densities contain a factor log Phi(x) that is evaluated as the log of a CDF value; it is -Inf once that value underflows: a skew-normal row far on its short side, an ex-Gaussian row far below its mean.
\item[Observed] skew\_normal mu = 0, sigma = 1, alpha = 10: y = -5 exact (-259.5392660824244), y = -8 and -9 -Inf. exgaussian mu = 0, sigma = 1, beta = 1: y = -36 exact (-617.0032275937984), y = -40 -Inf.
\item[Expected] -841.9599722745395 and -1110.717630363651 (skew normal), -765.1084420137538 (ex-Gaussian), with log Phi from R's \texttt{pnorm(\allowbreak{}x,\allowbreak{} log.\allowbreak{}p =\allowbreak{} TRUE)}; the control rows (y = 0.5) agree to 7e-16.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U27.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U27.out}.
\item[Fix] Evaluate the factor with an accurate log CDF: \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf(\allowbreak{}x)}, or \texttt{log(\allowbreak{}erfcx(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}x /\allowbreak{} sqrt 2) /\allowbreak{} 2) -\allowbreak{} x\textasciicircum{}2 /\allowbreak{} 2} for x \textless{} 0, instead of the log of \texttt{Phi} or \texttt{erfc}.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math}
\item[Known upstream] Not found for these log densities' lower tail; related work is open.
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3406} (open PR): Expanded numerical stability and performance for \texttt{std\_\allowbreak{}normal\_\allowbreak{}lcdf}, reused across distributions \& functions
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/pull/3443} (open PR): Compute skew\_normal\_lcdf and skew\_normal\_lccdf without cancellation in the tails
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/2803} (closed 2026-10-06): Fix Exponentially modified Gaussian overflows at lambda \textgreater{}= 40
\\ \#3443 is about the CDFs and \#2803 about another regime (large lambda), not these log densities' lower tail.
\end{description}

\subsection{U28: loo's \texttt{stacking\_\allowbreak{}weights(\allowbreak{})} stops short of the optimum (weights off by up to 3.7e-4, no exact zeros)}
\label{U28}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] loo: stacking\_weights(), loo\_model\_weights(method = "stacking"), brms: model\_weights(weights = "stacking"). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: loo 2.9.0, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] E05 (\#73); divergence D126. Stacking is withheld in AutoBayes pending a decision; on the frozen case \texttt{gauss\_\allowbreak{}loo\_\allowbreak{}compare\_\allowbreak{}x\_\allowbreak{}stacking} brms's weights are 1.04e-8 from the optimum.
\item[What] The stacking objective is maximised by \texttt{stats::constrOptim} (a log-barrier method) and the result returned at its tolerance, so the weights are near, not at, the optimum, and a model the optimum excludes keeps a small positive weight.
\item[Observed] Seeded pointwise elpd sets: \texttt{two\_\allowbreak{}nearly\_\allowbreak{}equal} loo (0.999630903495, 0.000369096505); \texttt{five\_\allowbreak{}200} up to 7e-5 off with 1.5e-7 on an excluded model; \texttt{four\_\allowbreak{}one\_\allowbreak{}dominated} 9.4e-6 off with 1.7e-8 on the excluded model; objective up to 2e-6 below the optimum's.
\item[Expected] (1, 0) for \texttt{two\_\allowbreak{}nearly\_\allowbreak{}equal}, exact zeros for excluded models, and the KKT optimum of \texttt{sum\_\allowbreak{}i log(\allowbreak{}sum\_\allowbreak{}k w\_\allowbreak{}k exp(\allowbreak{}lpd\_\allowbreak{}ik))} on the simplex (computed in the script by multiplicative updates and active-set Newton steps).
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U28.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U28.out}.
\item[Fix] Solve the stacking problem to its KKT conditions (\texttt{g\_\allowbreak{}k =\allowbreak{} sum\_\allowbreak{}i exp(\allowbreak{}lpd\_\allowbreak{}ik) /\allowbreak{} p\_\allowbreak{}i} equal to N on the support and at most N off it), e.g. by an active-set Newton method on the simplex, which gives exact zeros.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/loo}
\item[Known upstream] Known: an open issue to improve the optimiser and an open pull request with an active-set Newton method.
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/issues/119} (open): accelerate the optimization algorithm in stacking
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/412} (open PR): Compute stacking weights with an active-set Newton method
\\ loo 2.10.1 is on CRAN; it was not tested here (loo 2.9.0 installed).
\end{description}

\subsection{U29: \texttt{loo\_\allowbreak{}compare(\allowbreak{})} compares a PSIS-LOO result with a WAIC result without an error or a warning}
\label{U29}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] loo: loo\_compare(). Missing validation; reproduced. Versions: loo 2.9.0, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] D05 (\#58); divergence D93.
\item[What] A \texttt{waic} object is also of class \texttt{loo}, and \texttt{loo\_\allowbreak{}compare(\allowbreak{})} accepts it next to a \texttt{psis\_\allowbreak{}loo} object, naming the table's columns after the first argument's criterion, so a mixed table reads as a LOO comparison.
\item[Observed] \texttt{loo\_\allowbreak{}compare(\allowbreak{}loo(\allowbreak{}ll1),\allowbreak{} waic(\allowbreak{}ll2))} returns a table with columns \texttt{elpd\_\allowbreak{}loo}, \texttt{p\_\allowbreak{}loo}, \texttt{looic} and no warning.
\item[Expected] An error, or at least a warning, that the two results use different criteria.
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U29.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U29.out}.
\item[Fix] Check that all compared objects come from the same criterion (e.g. all \texttt{psis\_\allowbreak{}loo}, all \texttt{waic}, all \texttt{kfold}) and refuse or warn otherwise.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/loo}
\item[Known upstream] Not found in loo's NEWS or issue tracker (read-only searches).
\\ loo 2.10.0 changed \texttt{loo\_\allowbreak{}compare(\allowbreak{})}'s output (\#300); whether it now checks the criteria was not tested (loo 2.9.0 installed).
\end{description}

\subsection{U30: loo's MCSE of an observation's elpd\_loo is NaN once that elpd is below about -372}
\label{U30}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] loo: loo(), mcse\_elpd\_loo (pointwise and total). Inexact numerics; reproduced. Versions: loo 2.9.0, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] C07 (\#49); divergence D50.
\item[What] The Monte Carlo standard error of elpd\_loo\_i is NaN once its square on the probability scale underflows, and the total MCSE with it; elpd\_loo, p\_loo and k-hat are unaffected. Shifting the observation's log-likelihood by a constant shifts elpd\_loo\_i and leaves every other per-observation quantity unchanged, so its MCSE should not change either.
\item[Observed] 1000 draws x 5 observations, the fifth near -400: its \texttt{mcse\_\allowbreak{}elpd\_\allowbreak{}loo} is NaN and \texttt{print(\allowbreak{})} says "MCSE of elpd\_loo is NaN."
\item[Expected] 0.0134962534892, the MCSE of the same column shifted by +400 (whose elpd\_loo, -0.0836882186983, is the original's plus 400, and whose p\_loo and k-hat are identical).
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U30.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U30.out}.
\item[Fix] Evaluate the MCSE after subtracting \texttt{max\_\allowbreak{}s log p\_\allowbreak{}is} from the observation's log-likelihood (the MCSE is invariant to that shift), or carry the log-normal approximation's terms relative to \texttt{exp(\allowbreak{}elpd\_\allowbreak{}loo\_\allowbreak{}i)}, so that nothing squares \texttt{exp(\allowbreak{}elpd\_\allowbreak{}loo\_\allowbreak{}i)}.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/loo}
\item[Known upstream] Not found as such; an open issue on the MCSE and a merged accuracy change in the development version may cover it.
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/issues/245} (open): Improved mcse\_elpd\_loo
\\ \url{https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/pull/395} (merged 2026-09-15): Improve floating point accuracy
\\ PR \#395 is in loo's development version only (CRAN has 2.10.1); whether it fixes this was not tested.
\end{description}

\subsection{U31: A one-row model with \texttt{trunc(\allowbreak{})} (a per-row or a constant bound) cannot be built: rstan stops at data initialisation}
\label{U31}
\begin{description}[style=nextline, leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=2pt]
\item[Where] brms: trunc(lb = ), brm(), make\_standata(). Wrong result; reproduced. Versions: brms 2.23.0, rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.32.10, R 4.5.2.
\item[Found by] upstream log (U22). Found while writing U22, whose truncated rows use two identical rows for this reason.
\item[What] With a single data row, \texttt{make\_\allowbreak{}standata(\allowbreak{})} gives the truncation bound \texttt{lb} as a plain number (no dim) while the program declares it with length N = 1, so rstan refuses the data ("mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context ... variable name=lb; dims declared=(1); dims found=()") and \texttt{brm(\allowbreak{})} returns an object without a valid model. Rare in practice, but it breaks one-row checks and examples.
\item[Observed] \texttt{y \textbar{} trunc(\allowbreak{}lb =\allowbreak{} L) \textasciitilde{} 1} and \texttt{y \textbar{} trunc(\allowbreak{}lb =\allowbreak{} 1) \textasciitilde{} 1} with one row (y = 1.5, L = 1): the rstan error above at \texttt{brm(\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} chains =\allowbreak{} 0)}, then "the model object is not created or not valid" from \texttt{log\_\allowbreak{}prob}.
\item[Expected] A model whose log likelihood at mu = 0, sigma = 1 is \texttt{log phi(\allowbreak{}1.\allowbreak{}5) -\allowbreak{} log(\allowbreak{}1 -\allowbreak{} Phi(\allowbreak{}1))} = -0.2029168881954091, as the same model with two identical rows gives twice that (brms -0.4058337763908186) and a one-row model without truncation gives \texttt{log phi(\allowbreak{}1.\allowbreak{}5)} (brms -2.043938533204672, exact).
\item[Reproduce] \texttt{Rscript docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U31.R} from the repository root; it exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Output of one run: \texttt{docs/brms-parity/upstream/repro/U31.out}.
\item[Fix] Pass the bounds (and any other per-row data entry) to Stan as arrays of length N even when N = 1, e.g. with \texttt{as.\allowbreak{}array(\allowbreak{})}, as brms already does for the response.
\item[Belongs in] \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms}
\item[Known upstream] Not found for truncation bounds; the same kind of one-row failure was reported for an offset in 2018.
\\ \url{https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/545} (closed 2018-11-06): Can't sample when using offset with a single data point
\end{description}
